# Unwritten information is looked up {#sec-lookup}

## Rhyme plans {#sec-couplets}

Rhyming couplets are the flagship case of latent planning: the model commits to a rhyme
at the end of line 1 and realizes it at the end of line 2 [@lindsey2025biology;
@hanna2026latent]. We use the couplet prompts and chat format of @hanna2026latent and
repeat every run with the plain prompt of @ma2026plan (100 couplets per run; Appendix
@sec-app-couplets). The source is the last word of line 1, the donor a couplet from a
different rhyme group, and the target the position that predicts the first token of
line 2's last word, with the line-2 prefix fixed. The edit moves line 2 off its rhyme (at
most 2% of second lines still rhyme with the original, against 83 to 100% before the
edit) and onto the donor's rhyme in 27 to 95% of couplets. The emitted line-2 words
account for 13 to 25% of the total effect; the rest is persistence.

**Direct retrieval dominates, and relay is at most 1%.** @fig-couplets decomposes
persistence in all 21 runs. Direct retrieval of the rhyme word accounts for 76 to 95% of
persistence in every Qwen3 configuration (1.7B to 32B, chat and plain, instruct and base)
and 80 to 95% in Gemma 3 1B to 12B. The late lookup accounts for 1 to 13%. Relay along the
rest of the generated line is at most 1% of persistence in every run, by sufficiency in
all 21 and by necessity in the 17 where it was measured. Before running the larger
models we committed two criteria for the claim that relay grows with scale: the indirect
share must rise with log parameter count across Qwen3 1.7B to 32B, and the rise must come
from relay. The first holds (6.2 percentage points per decade, 95% interval [2.8, 9.6]);
the second fails (relay is \(-0.06\) to \(+0.16\), against persistence of 12 to 26). The
indirect share grows as the late lookup up to 8B and as the stored copy from 14B. Controls support the split (Appendix @sec-app-couplets): same-rhyme donors leave the
rhyme almost unchanged, the rhyme word matters two to three times more than any other
position of line 1, and the published feature steering of @hanna2026latent gives the
same split as the state edit (direct retrieval 90, 88 and 84% at 4B, 8B and 14B, against
91, 90 and 82%).

**Top:** composition of persistence from the sufficiency cells: direct retrieval of the

## The stored copy {#sec-storage}

Gemma 3 27B is the exception to retrieval dominance. Direct retrieval falls to 68% of
persistence with the chat prompt and 19% with the plain prompt, and two components
appear: a large interaction and a copy stored at the line's final token.

**It sits on the line's final token.** Resetting the tokens between the rhyme word and
line 2 one at a time locates the copy. In all five runs analysed, the line's final token
accounts for 90 to 100% of these tokens' summed necessity, and the chat-template tokens
hold almost nothing (Appendix @fig-sites). With the chat prompt this token is the comma
that ends line 1; with the plain prompt, the newline. The site is the last token of the
line, whatever that token is, which is where @lindsey2025biology observed Claude's rhyme
plan being formed.

**It emerges with scale, before instruction tuning.** In Qwen3 the copy is absent up to
8B (necessity at most 0.9% of persistence) and appears at 14B (8% with the chat prompt
and 16% with the plain prompt, by necessity), remaining at 32B (11% and 13%). In Gemma 3
it is small at 12B (1 to 3%) and present at 27B: 11% by necessity with the chat prompt
and, with the plain prompt, 37% by sufficiency and 74% by necessity, more than is read
from the rhyme word (19%), while relay stays at 1%. The base checkpoints we tested have
the copy wherever the matching instruct model does (Qwen3-14B-Base 16% against 13%;
Gemma 3 12B PT 5% against 2%), so it most likely arises in pretraining. Same-rhyme donors
remove it, so it encodes the rhyme.

**Where paths interact, sufficiency understates it.** In Gemma 3 27B with the chat
prompt, the copy alone moves the rhyme by only \(+0.68\), yet resetting it removes
\(+4.87\) [3.18, 6.73] of a persistence of \(+43.1\); the interaction is 29% of
persistence (Qwen3 at most 5%). The target combines the rhyme word and the copy, and
reads conflicting evidence when only one of them is edited: the copy is a redundant
second lookup site.

**Reconciling published accounts.** The heads near the end of line 2 that read the rhyme
word [@hanna2026latent] are direct retrieval with the late lookup; the plan found and
steered at the end of line 1 [@lindsey2025biology; @maar2026plan] is the stored copy of
larger models; the hand-off to the newline in Gemma 3 27B only [@ma2026plan] matches our
plain-format result; and no copy appears below 8B, as @jacopin2026improvisation finds.
Each account is correct for the configuration it studies (Appendix @sec-app-couplets).

**Why the stored copy is a lookup, not relay.** It passes through an intermediate
position, but it is written once into a fixed structural position next to the source,
read directly however much text intervenes, and does not move with generation: for a
monitor, one more place to read, not a path through the model's output.

## Computed values {#sec-computed}

Computed information is not present at any single token, which is where relay would seem
most useful (Appendix @sec-app-computed). In two-digit sums (Qwen3 1.7B to 32B, 104
items, a filler of 0 to 32 tokens before the answer), donor states at every position from
the question mark to the answer move the answer by at most 6.4% of the effect of donor
operand digits. Variable chains (`a = 23`, `b = a + 4`, ..., `What is e?`) make
recomputation at the answer costly and relay the natural path, so we designed them as a
second positive-control candidate for relay. They are not one. Donor states at every
position after the starting value together, a test that would detect a running value
stored redundantly, move the answer by at most 4.9% of the effect of editing the starting
value (32B, one update), and their interval includes zero at every size with five
updates, where a running value would help most. This is consistent with the answer
re-reading its visible sources; recomputation itself is not measured.

## Written values {#sec-emission}

When asked to compute each variable in order, the model writes the donor's values in 86
to 100% of items, and the answer follows the text. With the chain cut before its last
value, emission accounts for 83 to 101% of the effect at 1.7B to 32B, and the bypass
that re-reads the source stays below 17% (the 101%, at 32B with five updates, reflects a
slightly negative bypass). For a binary mediator such as the article *a* or *an* before
a planned noun, emission factorizes exactly into the change in what is written times the
written token's **leverage**, how much it matters to what follows (Appendix
@sec-app-computed). For the a/an planning features of @hanna2026latent in Qwen3-4B, 92
to 94% of their feature-specific effect on the planned noun travels through the
generated article, the bypass is at the level of random features, and the effect through
the article scales with leverage.
